messages:
alex: FYI after upgrading my laptop and running the new installer, `redwoodctl login` keeps trying SSH-agent auth before falling back to device code and the whole thing times out.
priya: hmm what platform + shell? any SSH_AGENT_PID set?
alex: macOS 14, zsh. I do use gpg-agent/ssh-agent for git. `env | grep SSH_AGENT` shows SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/run/user/1000/ssh-agent.sock.
alex: sequence: `redwoodctl login` -> CLI tries to use ssh-key auth -> ssh-agent rejects with `no identities` -> CLI immediately retries and spawns device-code browser flow, but the browser flow then errors with `interactive unavailable` because we're in headless remote session. it loops.
hendrix: can you paste `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 redwoodctl login`? I suspect we autodetect SSH keys when `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` exists and attempt token exchange using signed JWT.
alex: debug: "auth: found ssh key, attempting agent-sign" then "auth: agent sign failed: no identities" then "auth: falling back to device code" then "auth: device code: opening browser" then "auth: interactive not available" loop.
priya: sounds like an aggressive heuristic: trying SSH first is fine, but we should only try agent-sign if agent actually has keys. we currently call `agent.Sign` which returns an error but we treat that as retryable and immediately re-run full flow.
sam: workaround: `unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK` before running login so CLI won't try agent. or set `REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=device` to force device-code.
hendrix: good short-term. longer-term fix: (1) change detection to query agent for identities first with `ssh-add -l` equivalent, (2) if agent present but no identities, log a single WARN and skip agent flow, (3) cap automatic retries and surface a message "SSH agent present but has no identities; set REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=device or add a key to your agent." )ci-bot: opened issue devex#6721 "cli: avoid fruitless ssh-agent sign attempts during login" and linked PR draft.
priya: also add a small note to installer: if it detects that user has an SSH key file but agent is empty, offer a post-install hint: "You have SSH keys but your agent has no identities. If you prefer non-interactive auth, run `export REDWOOD_AUTH_METHOD=device`."
alex: confirmed unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK fixes it. thanks. would be great if the CLI did that check; this tripped a remote onboarding session earlier and confused the new hire.
hendrix: agreed. i'll prioritize the fix and add a unit test for agent-empty case.
sam: one more ask: when we fallback to device-code in a headless environment, don't auto-open the browser; instead print the URL and device code so remote sessions can copy-paste. current behavior assumes GUI.
hendrix: noted, adding `--no-browser` auto-detect when DISPLAY missing or CI env set.
priya: thanks team. marking as P2 and adding to next sprint. :white_check_mark:
